questions.name: Property Management
questions.objective: 6A General principles of property management agreements
questions.keyword: property manager as agent of owner
questions.text: A property manager who is hired to oversee a rental property on behalf of the owner serves primarily as:

answers.text: the owner's agent, owing fiduciary duties to the owner
the tenant's representative in all disputes with the landlord
an independent contractor with no agency relationship to either party
a neutral arbitrator between the owner and the tenants

explanations.a: A property manager acts as the owner's agent and owes fiduciary duties — loyalty, care, disclosure, and accounting — to the owner as principal.
explanations.b: The property manager represents the owner, not the tenants; tenants are the manager's customers, not clients.
explanations.c: A property management relationship is an agency relationship, not a purely independent contractor arrangement without fiduciary duties.
explanations.d: A property manager advocates for the owner's interests and is not a neutral arbitrator.

questions.name: Property Management
questions.objective: 6B Basic provisions of property management agreements
questions.text: A property management agreement typically specifies the manager's compensation as:

answers.text: a flat annual fee paid regardless of occupancy or rental income
a percentage of gross rents collected, often ranging from 4% to 12%
an hourly rate billed for each maintenance call responded to by the manager
a share of the property's equity appreciation at the end of each year

explanations.a: A flat annual fee regardless of collections is uncommon; it removes the manager's incentive to maximize occupancy.
explanations.b: Most residential property management agreements compensate the manager with a percentage of gross rents collected, aligning the manager's financial interest with the owner's income.
explanations.c: Hourly billing for maintenance calls is not the standard management compensation structure.
explanations.d: Equity appreciation sharing is not a typical property management fee arrangement.

questions.name: Property Management
questions.keyword: gross lease vs net lease expense responsibility
questions.text: Under a triple-net (NNN) lease, the tenant is responsible for paying:

answers.text: only the base rent, with all expenses paid by the landlord
base rent plus the landlord's mortgage payment on the building
base rent plus property taxes, building insurance, and maintenance costs
a percentage of gross sales in addition to a fixed base rent

explanations.a: Paying only base rent with the landlord covering all expenses describes a gross lease, not a triple-net lease.
explanations.b: A tenant is not responsible for the landlord's mortgage under a NNN lease.
explanations.c: In a triple-net (NNN) lease, the three 'nets' are property taxes, building insurance, and maintenance/operating costs, which the tenant pays in addition to the base rent.
explanations.d: A percentage of gross sales added to base rent describes a percentage lease, commonly used in retail — not a triple-net structure.

questions.name: Property Management
questions.objective: 6D Duties and obligations of the parties
questions.text: A property manager who deposits security deposits and rental income into a personal bank account rather than a separate trust account is:

answers.text: permitted to do so if the owner has signed a waiver of the trust account requirement
following standard practice when the portfolio has fewer than five units
complying with state law as long as a separate ledger is maintained
in violation of the duty of accounting and likely in breach of license law

explanations.a: An owner cannot waive trust account requirements imposed by state license law; the obligation is statutory.
explanations.b: No portfolio-size exemption excuses commingling client funds with personal funds.
explanations.c: A ledger does not substitute for proper separation of funds in a designated trust or escrow account.
explanations.d: Commingling client funds with a licensee's personal funds is a serious breach of the duty of accounting and typically a license law violation subject to discipline.

questions.name: Property Management
questions.text: A property manager conducts a rental market analysis primarily to:

answers.text: calculate the depreciation schedule for the owner's income tax return
determine competitive market rents and vacancy trends to set optimal rental rates
negotiate the property's assessed value with the county tax assessor
prepare the annual capital expenditure budget for major renovations

explanations.a: Depreciation schedules are prepared by the owner's accountant or tax advisor, not through a market analysis.
explanations.b: A rental market analysis surveys competing properties' rents, vacancy rates, and amenities to help the manager set competitive rental rates that maximize occupancy and income.
explanations.c: Tax assessments are handled by the local government; a market analysis does not affect the assessed value.
explanations.d: Capital expenditure budgeting is a separate function; a market analysis focuses on rental pricing and demand.

questions.name: Property Management
questions.text: Funds held in a property management trust account may generally be disbursed to the owner:

answers.text: after legitimate expenses and reserves have been deducted and an accounting rendered
only after the property has been sold and all tenants have vacated
at any time the manager chooses, since the manager controls the account
exclusively by wire transfer to a bank account in the owner's home state

explanations.a: A property manager disburses net rental proceeds to the owner after deducting authorized expenses, management fees, and reserves, and then provides the owner with a detailed accounting statement.
explanations.b: Disbursements to the owner occur on a regular cycle (monthly), not only upon sale of the property.
explanations.c: The manager does not have unlimited discretion over trust account funds; disbursements must follow the management agreement and proper accounting procedures.
explanations.d: The method of disbursement is a practical matter agreed upon in the management agreement; no law restricts payment to a specific state's bank.

questions.name: Property Management
questions.text: A property management agreement specifies that the manager may authorize repairs up to $500 without prior owner approval. A plumber quotes $750 for a necessary repair. The manager should:

answers.text: proceed with the repair immediately because tenant safety overrides all contractual limits
refuse to authorize any repair because the quote exceeds the manager's authority
reduce the scope of the repair to bring the cost under $500 without notifying the owner
contact the owner for approval before authorizing the repair, given that the cost exceeds the contractual limit

explanations.a: Except in a genuine emergency threatening immediate safety, the manager must follow the contractual spending limit and seek owner approval for amounts above it.
explanations.b: Refusing all action is not the correct approach; the manager should seek owner approval rather than simply decline.
explanations.c: Arbitrarily reducing the repair scope without consulting the owner could result in an inadequate fix and would still circumvent the proper approval process.
explanations.d: When a repair exceeds the manager's authorized spending limit, the manager must obtain the owner's approval before proceeding, except in a genuine emergency.

questions.name: Property Management
questions.text: When a tenant refuses to vacate after receiving a valid notice to quit, the landlord's legally required next step is to:

answers.text: change the locks and remove the tenant's belongings from the premises
reduce the tenant's utility services to encourage the tenant to leave voluntarily
file an unlawful detainer (dispossessory) action in court and obtain a writ of possession
demand that the property manager personally escort the tenant off the premises

explanations.a: Self-help eviction — changing locks or removing a tenant's belongings — is illegal in virtually all states and exposes the landlord to significant liability.
explanations.b: Cutting off utilities to force a tenant out is retaliatory and illegal in most jurisdictions.
explanations.c: The proper legal process for removing a holdover tenant is to file an unlawful detainer (dispossessory) action, obtain a court judgment, and have the sheriff enforce the writ of possession.
explanations.d: A property manager has no legal authority to physically remove a tenant; only a court order enforced by law enforcement authorizes eviction.

questions.name: Property Management
questions.objective: 6A General principles of property management agreements
questions.text: In most states, a person who manages rental property for others for compensation is required to hold:

answers.text: a general contractor's license from the state licensing board
a property appraiser's certification from an approved appraisal organization
a real estate broker's or property manager's license issued by the state
no license, because property management is exempt from real estate licensing laws

explanations.a: A general contractor's license covers construction work, not property management services.
explanations.b: Appraisal certification relates to property valuation, not management.
explanations.c: Most states require a person who manages real property for others for compensation to hold a real estate broker's license or a separate property manager's license.
explanations.d: Property management for compensation is not generally exempt from licensing requirements; managing others' property without a license is typically illegal.

questions.name: Property Management
questions.objective: 6B Basic provisions of property management agreements
questions.text: A property management agreement should clearly define the scope of the manager's authority in order to:

answers.text: allow the manager to purchase additional investment properties on the owner's behalf
guarantee that all tenants will pay rent on time throughout the management period
exempt the manager from all liability for tenant actions during the management term
prevent disputes about what actions the manager may take without seeking owner approval

explanations.a: Purchasing investment properties would require a separate and explicit grant of authority; it is not a standard property management function.
explanations.b: No agreement can guarantee timely rent payment by tenants.
explanations.c: A management agreement does not provide blanket immunity from liability for the manager's actions.
explanations.d: Clearly defining the scope of authority prevents misunderstandings and disputes between the owner and manager over what decisions require owner approval.

questions.name: Property Management
questions.objective: 6D Duties and obligations of the parties
questions.text: Under a property management agreement, the owner's primary obligation to the property manager is to:

answers.text: personally approve every lease renewal regardless of the terms agreed upon
provide sufficient operating funds and timely decisions to allow the manager to perform
indemnify all tenants for any injury occurring on the property regardless of cause
guarantee the manager a minimum income even if the property remains vacant

explanations.a: If the management agreement authorizes the manager to renew leases within defined parameters, personal owner approval for each renewal is not required.
explanations.b: The owner must provide the operating reserves and timely decision-making that allows the manager to maintain the property, pay expenses, and perform management duties effectively.
explanations.c: Blanket tenant indemnification is not a standard owner obligation under a management agreement.
explanations.d: A guaranteed minimum income to the manager regardless of vacancies is not a standard term in property management agreements.

questions.name: Property Management
questions.text: State law typically requires a landlord or property manager to hold a tenant's security deposit in:

answers.text: a separate account and provide the tenant with written notice of where the deposit is held
the landlord's general operating account to facilitate quick disbursement at lease end
a federally insured CD in the landlord's name, with interest payable to the landlord
cash kept in a safe at the managed property for easy access by the tenant

explanations.a: Most state security deposit statutes require that deposits be held in a separate account and that the tenant receive written notice of the depository institution and account information.
explanations.b: Commingling security deposits with operating funds is prohibited; a separate account is required.
explanations.c: State law does not typically mandate a CD, and interest requirements vary by state; many states require interest to be paid to the tenant, not the landlord.
explanations.d: Keeping cash in a safe at the property is not an acceptable security deposit custodial method.

questions.name: Property Management
questions.text: To avoid fair housing violations when screening rental applicants, a property manager should:

answers.text: ask each applicant about their national origin to ensure a diverse tenant mix
require larger security deposits from applicants who have children
approve the first applicant who meets the minimum income threshold
apply the same written qualifying criteria consistently to all applicants

explanations.a: Asking about national origin in the screening process is discriminatory and violates the Fair Housing Act.
explanations.b: Requiring larger deposits based on familial status (having children) is a Fair Housing Act violation.
explanations.c: While consistency is important, a manager need not approve the first applicant; the manager may accept the best-qualified applicant, provided criteria are applied uniformly.
explanations.d: Using written, objective, consistently applied qualifying criteria — such as income-to-rent ratio, credit score, and rental history — protects the manager against fair housing complaints and ensures equal treatment.

questions.name: Property Management
questions.text: Replacing a worn carpet throughout an entire apartment with new flooring is BEST classified as:

answers.text: a routine maintenance expense deducted from the current month's rents
a security deposit deduction charged directly to the outgoing tenant
a capital improvement that adds value and is depreciated over time for tax purposes
a tenant improvement allowance funded by the incoming tenant

explanations.a: Replacing all flooring is not routine maintenance; it is a capital expenditure that extends the property's useful life.
explanations.b: Normal wear and tear — including carpet that has reached the end of its useful life — cannot be charged to a security deposit; only damage beyond normal wear is chargeable.
explanations.c: A full carpet replacement is a capital improvement because it extends the property's useful life and adds value; it is depreciated over its useful life for income tax purposes.
explanations.d: Tenant improvement allowances are typically negotiated in commercial leases; they are not how residential landlords handle floor replacement.

questions.name: Property Management
questions.keyword: notice to quit required before eviction
questions.text: Before filing an eviction lawsuit against a non-paying tenant, a landlord must generally first:

answers.text: provide the tenant with a written notice to pay the overdue rent or vacate within a specified period
obtain the property manager's notarized certification that rent is delinquent
file a mechanic's lien against the tenant's personal property
report the delinquency to all three national credit bureaus

explanations.a: Most states require a landlord to serve a written pay-or-quit notice giving the tenant a statutory period (commonly 3 to 14 days) to pay the overdue rent or vacate before an eviction action may be filed.
explanations.b: A property manager's notarized certification is not a legal prerequisite for filing an eviction; the required step is the pay-or-quit notice to the tenant.
explanations.c: A mechanic's lien secures payment for labor and materials on real property; it is not a pre-eviction requirement.
explanations.d: Credit bureau reporting is a collection tool, not a statutory prerequisite to an eviction proceeding.

questions.name: Property Management
questions.text: A retail tenant pays a base rent of $3,000 per month plus 5% of annual gross sales exceeding $600,000. If the tenant's annual gross sales are $800,000, what is the tenant's total annual rent?

explanations.a: $36,000 is base rent only ($3,000 × 12); it ignores the percentage rent component.
explanations.c: $40,000 does not correspond to the correct calculation using the given figures.
explanations.d: $76,000 would result from applying 5% to all $800,000 in sales rather than only the overage above $600,000.
